headline: Luzardo, Sale to start Phillies-Braves Wild Card opener
recap: The Phillies closed out the regular season Sunday with a 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays at Citizens Bank Park. Bryson Stott's double in the first inning scored Kyle Schwarber for an early 1-0 lead, and Philadelphia broke it open in the second when J.T. Realmuto's double drove in Edmundo Sosa before Schwarber's own double scored both Realmuto and Trea Turner to make it 4-0. Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca homered in the fifth to trim the deficit to 4-1, but the Phillies answered right back in the bottom half: Bryce Harper hit his 29th home run, Brandon Marsh added a sacrifice fly to score Stott, and Sosa homered for his ninth to push the lead to 7-1. DeLuca's second homer of the game and a Victor Mesa Jr. single that scored Jorge Mateo cut the final margin to 7-3 in the seventh. Zack Wheeler earned the win, allowing one run over six innings with five strikeouts, while Nick Martinez took the loss for Tampa Bay.

The win closed the season at 88-74, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-champion Atlanta Braves, and left Philadelphia on a one-game winning streak. The Phillies enter the postseason as a National League Wild Card.

Philadelphia opens the best-of-three NL Wild Card Series on the road against the Braves at Truist Park today, with first pitch scheduled for 2:00 p.m. ET. Jesús Luzardo is the probable starter for the Phillies against Atlanta's Chris Sale. The Braves are a -205 favorite on the moneyline, with the Phillies at +168.
